summary.headline: Gabriel India Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 15.5% YoY to INR1,426 crore, while EBITDA grew only 2% to INR124 crore; Project Jupiter approved.
summary.overview: Board approved Project Jupiter: a 28.99% stake in HL Mando Anand (INR2,231 crore, of which INR1,881 crore via share allotment and INR350 crore cash) and a 30% minus 1 share stake in HL Klemove India (USD 98.44 million) as a JV in ADAS. Standalone revenue rose 19% YoY to INR1,274 crore and standalone EBITDA rose 7% to INR107 crore, with margin at 8.4%. Consolidated EBITDA margin was 8.7%, and PBT rose 6% to INR133 crore, with share of equity-accounted JVs up 10% to INR43 crore. Management flagged commodity-driven material cost pressure and delayed price recoveries, and a sunroof volume shortfall tied to a Hyundai production disruption. Financing plans include about INR1,000-1,600 crore of debt and a targeted debt-equity ratio near 1:1.

financial_highlights.metric: Share of PBT from equity-accounted investees (Dana Anand, Henkel Anand, SK Enmove Gabriel)

financial_highlights.change: management cited a decline of roughly 80-100 bps per analyst question

segments.name: Standalone suspension business
segments.commentary: Management cited healthy demand in core suspension and continued aftermarket growth, plus Anchemco contribution from the restructuring. Passenger vehicle sales grew about 5.5% vs PV industry production up 17%; PV revenue share fell from 24% to 20%, which management attributed to model mix and lower wallet share at a large customer.

segments.name: Sunroof (HL Mando-linked, in HL Klemove/HL Mando perimeter)
segments.commentary: A supplier issue at Hyundai Mobis hit Hyundai Creta production; management estimated 15,000-20,000 units lost in Q1, expected to be recovered in Q1-Q2 with no FY27 budget shortfall.

segments.name: HL Mando Anand (target, 28.99%)
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover about INR5,886 crore, PAT INR358 crore, net worth INR1,924 crore. Non-Korean customers now about 40% of business (Hyundai, Kia, Tata Motors, Mahindra, Maruti Suzuki).

segments.name: HL Klemove India (JV, 30% minus 1 share)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue above INR1,000 crore (unaudited) and adjusted EBITDA about INR129 crore. Customers include Hyundai/Kia-linked and Mahindra and Tata Motors programmes; manufacturing in Chennai. Content per vehicle estimated at INR20,000-70,000.

segments.name: Henkel Anand and CY Myutec (JVs/subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Management said Henkel's FY26 profit declined due to commodity cost changes linked to the Middle East situation, with recoveries accounted for on an actual basis. Analyst noted subdued growth and profit decline in FY26 for both entities.

guidance_outlook: Group revenue target of INR50,000 crore by FY30, with Gabriel as the main growth vehicle for Anand Group automotive components.
Post Project Jupiter, Gabriel will account for about 70% of Anand Group revenue; the remaining 30% will be brought in at an appropriate time with no fixed timeline.
Export share is currently 7-8% of business, with a stated target of 10% over the coming timeline; opportunities cited in shock absorbers, solar and e-bikes.
Debt-equity ratio expected at about 1:1 after both transactions close (currently below 0.1-0.2).
Interest cost implications to be disclosed from Q2 FY27 onward, once instrument mix is finalised.
HL Klemove: first tranche of USD 73.83 million due on or before 15 September 2026; balance USD 24.61 million within 18 months of signing definitive agreements.
risks_watch: Standalone margin pressure from commodity inflation; the recovery lag from customers needs to narrow in Q2 FY27.
Sunroof volume recovery of 15,000-20,000 units from Hyundai Creta disruption must be confirmed in Q2.
Leverage rising toward 1:1 debt-equity on about INR1,000-1,600 crore of new debt; interest cost not yet disclosed.
HL Klemove FY26 figures are unaudited; the margin and growth track record needs verification.
Henkel and CY Myutec profit declines in FY26 and the Eaton Mobility merger with Dana (not yet closed) could affect JV performance.
Passenger vehicle underperformance vs industry (5.5% vs 17%) and wallet share loss at a key customer.
Pending stock exchange listing approval for Project Rise.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and forward-looking on the Anand Group consolidation and the INR50,000 crore FY30 target. It was more cautious and vague on specifics: it declined to give numerical HL Klemove growth or export guidance, and deferred interest cost and some regulatory questions to later.
key_quotes: So debt equity should be 1:1, once we close our transactions -- both these transactions, the debt equity from the '26-'27 perspective should be 1:1.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked how Gabriel's relationship with HL Group began and what drives it.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the HL Mando relationship dates to 1996, starting with brakes, then suspension and steering, and that the company is now around INR5,500 crore+ in revenue, close to INR6,000 crore in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked for the medium-term growth outlook and key customers for HL Klemove.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers, citing a strong pipeline with Mahindra and Tata Motors business on new launches, and said the per-vehicle content makes the revenue opportunity large.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the sunroof volume shortfall and margin pressure in standalone business.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the standalone margin decline came from commodity-driven material cost inflation and recovery lag from customers; sunroof loss was about 15,000-20,000 units in Q1, with recovery expected in Q1 and Q2 and no FY27 shortfall in budget.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked why the PV business underperformed the market and why its revenue share fell from 24% to 20%.
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to model mix (absence from some strong UV platforms) and lower wallet share at the biggest customer; smaller cars grew faster than market.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the debt-equity outlook and interest cost for FY27.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the debt-equity ratio would be about 1:1 after both deals close, versus less than 0.1 to 0.2 currently; interest cost is still being worked out and will be disclosed from next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about Gabriel's plans for the remaining 30% of Anand Group revenue after Project Jupiter.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Gabriel will reach about 70% of group sales after Mando, with the balance to be brought in at an appropriate time with no timeline given.

capex_capacity: Management said capex spans multiple locations: largest plant around Hosur, the Khandsa (Gurgaon) plant expansion, and the Sanand plant expansion, plus technology investment in the suspension business.

An analyst cited an INR180 crore expansion reported in media; management did not confirm the figure but described the spend as a combination of plant expansions and new technology investment in suspension.
Management said the company is funding working capital and capex from internal accruals for now, with short-term facilities available to cover the first HL Klemove tranche due by September 2026.

Debt raise: shareholder approval sought for up to about INR1,600 crore of debt; short and medium-term requirement about INR1,000 crore; CFO later referred to raising about INR800 crore at a comfortable stage.
Management said there are no plans for a QIP currently; the Project Jupiter acquisitions will be funded through a mix of debt and equity.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 industry production growth YoY: 2-wheelers +23% (scooters +32%, motorcycles +18%); passenger vehicles +17% (utility vehicles +21%); commercial vehicles +15% (LCVs +21%, MHCV +6%).

Standalone PV business grew about 5.5% YoY, below the PV industry growth figure; the analyst cited 15%, and management did not dispute it. PV share of standalone revenue fell from 24% to 20%, which management attributed to model mix (weak UV platforms, no presence on some high-performing UV models) and lower wallet share at the biggest customer. Smaller cars grew faster than market.
Standalone revenue grew 19% YoY on healthy core suspension demand, aftermarket growth and Anchemco contribution from the restructuring.
Standalone margin pressure from commodity-driven material cost inflation; recoveries from customers lag, with some settled and others still under discussion.

Sunroof: Hyundai Creta output was cut by a supplier issue at Hyundai Mobis; management estimated 15,000-20,000 units lost in Q1, with customer confident of recovering in Q1 and Q2 and no FY27 budget shortfall.

Henkel profit fell in FY26 due to commodity cost changes linked to the Middle East situation; recoveries accounted for on an actual basis. Management expects the impact to flow through to future profitability.
Export share is 7-8% of business; target of 10% over the coming timeline, with opportunities cited in shock absorbers, solar and e-bikes.
HL Mando non-Korean customers now about 40% of its business (Mahindra, Tata Motors, Maruti Suzuki, Hyundai, Kia). HL Klemove content per vehicle estimated at INR20,000-70,000 per vehicle.

adds.what: Plant expansions around Hosur, Khandsa (Gurgaon) and Sanand plus suspension technology investment (capex figure of INR180 crore cited by analyst, not confirmed

growth.why: Management targets INR50,000 crore group revenue by FY30 with Gabriel as growth vehicle, backed by Project Jupiter acquisitions and unquantified Hosur/Khandsa/Sanand plant expansions, export target of 10%, and healthy core suspension demand; however, the FY30 target lacks specific timelines or order numbers for the capacity, and the standalone PV business lagged industry growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin fell to 8.4% (down roughly 80-100 bps per analyst) on commodity inflation and lagging customer recoveries, with consolidated EBITDA up only 2% vs revenue up 15.5%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management described plant expansions at Hosur, Khandsa (Gurgaon) and Sanand plus suspension technology investment, though the INR180 crore figure was an analyst citation not confirmed by management and no commissioning dates were given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Sunroof volumes of 15,000-20,000 Creta units lost in Q1 are expected to recover in Q1-Q2, healthy core suspension demand and aftermarket growth drove standalone revenue up 19%, but standalone PV grew only about 5.5% vs industry PV production up 17%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is already spanning Hosur, Khandsa and Sanand plus suspension technology, and Project Jupiter plus about INR1,000-1,600 crore of new debt is being raised; the utilisation level was not disclosed, so the capex call rests on stated plans rather than a utilisation read.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the INR50,000 crore FY30 group revenue target but declined to give numerical HL Klemove or export guidance, and Q1 EBITDA growth was only 2%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Commodity-driven cost inflation and delayed price recoveries hit standalone margin (8.4%), and the Q2 recovery lag and sunroof catch-up are unconfirmed, with interest cost on the new debt not yet disclosed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management cited opportunities in shock absorbers, solar and e-bikes for exports and a strong Mahindra and Tata Motors pipeline on new launches at HL Klemove, but no specific product launch dates were given.

rows.label: HL Klemove Mahindra/Tata new-launch pipeline
rows.why: Management cited a strong pipeline with Mahindra and Tata Motors new launches and content per vehicle of INR20,000-70,000, but declined to quantify growth.

rows.label: Debt-equity rising to about 1:1
rows.why: Debt-equity is below 0.1-0.2 today and is expected at about 1:1 after both Project Jupiter deals, funded by INR1,000-1,600 crore of debt plus INR1,881 crore of share allotment.

rows.label: HL Klemove first tranche USD 73.83 million
rows.why: First tranche of the USD 98.44 million HL Klemove JV investment is due by 15 September 2026, with short-term facilities arranged to cover it.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Anand Group consolidation and the INR50,000 crore FY30 target but cautious and vague on HL Klemove growth, export numbers, and interest cost; analysts pressed on standalone margin decline, PV underperformance (5.5% vs 17%), and leverage.
